posts.text:
SCHUMER VOWS TO END IRAN WAR USING DEMOCRATS' NEW CONGRESSIONAL MAJORITY

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer declared that Democrats will move to end the Iran war, citing Congress's constitutional authority over federal spending.

“We are going to end the war,” Schumer said Wednesday, emphasizing that some Republicans already support efforts to halt the conflict.

Congress previously passed measures calling for an end to hostilities, including a September House resolution backed by seven Republicans.

posts.text:
This is highly unusual:

The S&P 500 is trading more than 2 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, the first such occurrence since April.

Such a reading puts the S&P 500 in historically extreme oversold territory.

At the same time, only ~17% of the index’s stocks are now oversold, near its lowest proportion since July.

Meanwhile, ~47% of stocks are now overbought, the highest proportion since early February. 

This figure has more than doubled since the start of October as many stocks have rallied beneath the surface.

The broader market looks far healthier than the S&P 500's recent performance suggests.

posts.text:
The era of massive Big Tech stock buybacks is over.

Combined buybacks by Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Microsoft, $MSFT, Meta, $META, and Oracle, $ORCL, fell to $4.4 billion in Q3 2026, the lowest since Q3 2017.

Share repurchases have dropped -90% since the ~$45.9 billion peak recorded in Q4 2021.

This also marks the 3rd consecutive quarter with buybacks below $5.0 billion.

This comes as Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle have not purchased their own stock in 2026.

By comparison, combined buybacks by these Big Tech companies stood at +$33.0 billion in Q1 2026.

AI spending is coming at the expense of Big Tech buybacks.
